subject: general
question: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop is directly proportional to ______________.

options.text: the square of the radius of the circular loop
the current flowing through the loop
inverse of current flowing through the loop
the square of the current flowing through the loop

solution:
The correct answer is __**the current flowing through the loop**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnetic field at the center of a current-carrying circular loop is determined using **Ampere’s Law** or **Biot-Savart Law**. It is given by the formula: **B = (μ₀ * I) / (2 * R)**, where:

 
 
• **B**: Magnetic field at the center (measured in Tesla).
 
• **μ₀**: Permeability of free space (4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A).
 
• **I**: Current flowing through the loop.
 
• **R**: Radius of the loop.
 
 
 
• From the formula, it is evident that the magnetic field **B is directly proportional to the current (I)**. Hence, an increase in current will lead to a proportional increase in the magnetic field.
 
• The radius of the loop affects the magnetic field inversely. However, the question specifically asks about direct proportionality, which is only true for the current flowing through the loop.
 
• The other options, such as the square of the radius or the square of the current, are not correct because the magnetic field does not depend on these quantities in that manner.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is the current flowing through the loop.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biot-Savart Law:**

 
 
• The Biot-Savart law describes the magnetic field produced by a current element. It states that the magnetic field (dB) due to a small segment of current (IdL) at a point is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the segment and the point.
 
• Mathematically: **dB = (μ₀/4π) * (I * dL × r̂) / r²**.
 
 
 
• **Ampere’s Law:**
 
 
• Ampere’s Law relates the integrated magnetic field around a closed loop to the total electric current passing through the loop.
 
• It is expressed as: **∮B·dl = μ₀I**, where I is the current enclosed by the loop.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Radius:**
 
 
• The magnetic field at the center is inversely proportional to the radius of the loop. If the radius increases, the field decreases and vice versa.
 
• This relationship is evident from the formula: **B = (μ₀ * I) / (2 * R)**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Magnetic Fields in Circular Loops:**
 
 
• Used in electromagnets for generating strong magnetic fields.
 
• Widely applied in electric motors, MRI machines, and particle accelerators.
 
 
 
• **Units and Constants:**
 
 
• Magnetic field (B) is measured in **Tesla (T)**.
 
• Permeability of free space (μ₀) has a value of **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** The square of the radius of the circular loop is not involved in the formula for the magnetic field. Thus, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Option 3:** The inverse of the current is incorrect because the magnetic field is directly proportional to the current.
 
• **Option 4:** The square of the current does not influence the magnetic field; hence, this is also incorrect.
